briefs.title: Signal Before Customs Clears
briefs.hook: Service the second I touched down. Still not over it.
briefs.customer_quote_source: I had service the second I touched down. I'm still not over how easy it was to use
briefs.target_segment: First-time international travelers anxious about landing without connectivity
briefs.script_concept: POV shot from a plane window descending into a foreign city. Phone screen fills frame — the signal bar flicks on, maps load instantly, a WhatsApp notification pops. Creator turns camera to face: 'That's it. Literally that.' Cut to black. White text: 'Holafly. Connected before you clear customs.'
briefs.why_this_wins: It dramatizes the single highest-anxiety moment of international travel — the landing — and resolves it in under five seconds, making the payoff feel physical and immediate.

briefs.title: They Were Jealous
briefs.hook: My friends were jealous of my signal. Abroad.
briefs.customer_quote_source: Some of my family members and friends were actually kind of jealous that I was getting better service than their carrier provided.
briefs.target_segment: Millennial and Gen Z group travelers who share trips on social media
briefs.script_concept: Left half of screen: a traveler hunched over a café table, mouthing the wifi password to a waiter, staring at a loading spinner. Right half: same destination, different traveler — uploading a reel, on a video call, navigating without breaking stride. No voiceover. Just ambient sound and the real quote appearing as a text overlay. Final frame: 'One of us had Holafly.'
briefs.cta: Don't be the one hunting wifi.
briefs.why_this_wins: It reframes connectivity as social currency rather than utility, making the ad feel like travel content and the product feel like a status move.

briefs.title: Too Easy to Be Real
briefs.hook: I Googled if I set it up wrong. It was just done.
briefs.customer_quote_source: It was so easy I thought I did it wrong. Seamless eSIM for my first international trip! Worked the entire time with 0 issues.
briefs.format: 60s UGC testimonial video, mid-funnel YouTube or TikTok
briefs.target_segment: Tech-hesitant travelers who have never used an eSIM and fear the setup
briefs.script_concept: Creator sits at a kitchen table, passport next to them, speaking directly to camera: 'I am not a tech person. At all.' Screen recording plays — three taps, QR scan, done in under two minutes. Creator looks up: 'I literally searched if I'd missed a step.' Cut to trip footage — maps loading, stories uploading, a WhatsApp call from a rooftop. No jargon. No diagrams. Just disbelief that became delight.
briefs.cta: Set up in minutes. Travel without limits.
briefs.why_this_wins: Leading with self-doubt that collapses into relief mirrors the exact internal journey of every hesitant buyer, making conversion feel like a natural conclusion.

briefs.title: Unlimited Means the Job Gets Done
briefs.hook: My whole job runs on data. Holafly never flinched.
briefs.customer_quote_source: As a content creator I love using Holafly to have unlimited data to everywhere I go. It's a content creators' must!
briefs.format: 45s talking-head UGC + b-roll, YouTube pre-roll or Instagram Reels
briefs.target_segment: Travel content creators, digital nomads, and remote workers traveling internationally
briefs.script_concept: Creator speaks from a scenic location abroad, phone in hand showing data usage stats — gigabytes consumed, plan still active. 'My last provider throttled me on day three. Mid-upload.' Cut to b-roll: posting a reel from a beach, a Zoom call from a mountain café, navigating a foreign metro. Back to creator: 'Holafly has never once slowed me down.' The data usage screen lingers on screen. No fluff. Just proof.
briefs.why_this_wins: It speaks to a high-stakes professional pain point and backs every claim with visible on-screen evidence, turning a testimonial into a credibility demonstration.

briefs.title: One eSIM. Seven Countries. Zero Swaps.
briefs.hook: France, Spain, Belgium. One eSIM. Absolute success.
briefs.customer_quote_source: Lo mejor que han creado para los travelers. Francia, España, Bélgica. Un éxito absoluto!!
briefs.target_segment: European multi-destination travelers and Latin American tourists planning grand tours
briefs.script_concept: Each slide is designed as a passport stamp — the country name stamped bold, a real traveler photo behind it, a one-line customer quote from that destination, and a signal-strength screenshot in the corner. Slide 1: France. Slide 2: Spain. Slide 3: Belgium. Slide 4: Germany. Slide 5: Italy. Final slide breaks the stamp format with stark white: 'One eSIM. Every country. Zero swaps.' The traveler's voice carries the whole carousel — no telecom language anywhere.
briefs.cta: Plan your route. One eSIM covers it.
briefs.why_this_wins: The passport-stamp format is native to travel culture and transforms a functional benefit into a visually iconic, share-worthy story that feels earned rather than sold.

briefs.title: The Wifi Hunt Is Over
briefs.hook: I ran the whole trip looking for wifi. Had Holafly the whole time.
briefs.customer_quote_source: I ran around the entire trip looking for free wifi — the whole time I had Holafly eSIM on my phone
briefs.format: 30s vertical UGC comedy video, TikTok and Reels
briefs.target_segment: Budget travelers and first-timers who rely on free wifi abroad without realizing the hidden cost in time and stress
briefs.script_concept: Creator reenacts the wifi hunt in fast-forward: sprinting to a café, mispronouncing the password, staring at a spinning wheel, missing a turn, walking an extra block, asking a stranger. Cut hard to them sitting still, calm, phone out: 'I had Holafly in my pocket the whole time. I just never activated it.' Beat. Then a 20-second screen recording of the activation. Tone is self-roasting and funny — the humor is the hook, the activation is the close.
briefs.why_this_wins: It makes prospects laugh at a pain they have already lived, which collapses defenses and makes the solution feel obvious rather than pitched.

briefs.title: Better Signal Than the Locals
briefs.hook: Better service than my European friends. In Europe.
briefs.customer_quote_source: It has better service than my European friends do in many places.
briefs.format: Full-bleed editorial static ad, display and paid social
briefs.target_segment: North American and Latin American travelers heading to Europe
briefs.script_concept: Full-bleed photograph of a stunning European street — golden hour, no people, pure atmosphere. Overlaid in bold editorial type: 'Better signal than the locals.' Sub-copy below, smaller: 'No roaming fees. No physical SIM. Full bars from the moment you land.' Bottom right corner: a testimonial badge with the real quote, five stars, and a first-name attribution. The aesthetic is travel magazine — not a telecom banner. Nothing about plans or pricing. Just the claim and the proof.
briefs.why_this_wins: Flipping the expectation — a foreign visitor outperforming locals on their own turf — creates instant intrigue and a brand memory that no feature list could manufacture.

briefs.title: I Stopped Comparing
briefs.hook: I don't even consider other eSIM providers anymore.
briefs.customer_quote_source: I don't even consider other eSIM providers.
briefs.format: 60s interview-style testimonial video, YouTube and CTV
briefs.target_segment: Consideration-stage travelers actively comparing eSIM options and looking for a reason to commit
briefs.script_concept: Talking-head interview, warmly lit, no logo visible yet. Real customer speaks: 'First trip I was nervous. Second trip I was confident. By the fourth trip I set it up in my sleep.' Pause. Direct to camera: 'I don't even consider other providers.' No pitch follows. Camera slowly pulls back to reveal a Holafly screen on their phone. Super appears: 'Trusted in 170+ destinations worldwide.' Silence holds for two seconds. Fade to logo.
briefs.why_this_wins: In a crowded comparison market, 'I stopped comparing' is more persuasive than any feature list because it signals the decision is already settled — and invites the viewer to reach the same conclusion.

briefs.title: Phone Works. Brain Rests.
briefs.hook: Using my phone exactly like home. Stress just... left.
briefs.customer_quote_source: To be able to use my phone exactly the way I would at home while traveling took so much stress off of my shoulders
briefs.format: 45s cinematic UGC video, Instagram Reels and YouTube pre-roll
briefs.target_segment: Anxious first-time international travelers, parents traveling with family, solo travelers for whom connectivity is a safety need
briefs.script_concept: Opens on a traveler's face at an airport gate — tight, nervous, headphones in. Internal monologue in text overlay: 'What if I can't find my hotel. What if I can't call anyone. What if I get lost.' Plane lands. Phone screen shows signal, maps open, WhatsApp loads. The traveler's shoulders physically drop. Wide shot of them walking through a foreign city, completely present — no phone-hunting, no squinting at screens, just living the trip. Final line over a still frame: 'Your phone works like home. Your mind gets to be somewhere else.'
briefs.cta: Travel calm. Activate before you fly.
briefs.why_this_wins: It names the invisible emotional tax of international travel that every traveler carries but no telecom brand ever acknowledges, making Holafly feel like it actually understands the human behind the phone.

briefs.title: Cheap Cost Me More
briefs.hook: I tried saving money on connectivity abroad. Here's what it cost.
briefs.customer_quote_source: Holafly is more expensive, but well worth it. Was only esim I tried with continuous and ubiquitous reception.
briefs.format: 45s creator video with on-screen text, YouTube pre-roll and TikTok
briefs.target_segment: Price-sensitive but experience-driven travelers who have been burned by cheaper connectivity options
briefs.script_concept: Creator opens deadpan to camera: 'I tried saving twenty dollars on my eSIM. Here is what that decision actually cost me.' Rapid-fire text cards hit the screen: missed reservation because maps wouldn't load, forty minutes wandering in the wrong direction, roaming charges that wiped out the savings, a near-emergency with no way to call. No brand names. Then a hard cut to calm trip footage. Creator back on screen: 'I switched to Holafly. More expensive? Yes. Worth every single cent.' The real customer quote appears as a stamped testimonial. Final frame: the math — eSIM cost versus what a dead zone actually costs you.
briefs.why_this_wins: It proactively dismantles the only real purchase objection — price — by making the hidden cost of the cheap alternative feel more expensive, letting a real customer voice seal the deal.

raw_analyses.title: Frustrating
raw_analyses.content:
I used Holafly last year in Germany and it was very good, which is why I kept trying them. But lately, it’s been frustrating. In Canada (Vancouver and Whistler, BC), speeds were under 3 Mbps while my T-Mobile plan was nearly 100 Mbps. They used China Mobile as the carrier, and I’m not comfortable with a PRC-based company potentially accessing my data. Tech support had me switch settings but it didn’t really help. When I asked for a refund, they ghosted me.

Now in Europe, I’m using their Global unlimited eSIM. It works but speeds are again very low – around 25-30 Mbps while T-Mobile gives me nearly 300 Mbps with great uploads.

Worst part was trying to buy an eSIM for my wife. I spent over 2.5 hours on support chats, got charged three times ($58 each), and never received a single eSIM. Now I have to waste time disputing these charges with my credit card company. Support takes hours to respond and often cancels chats before anything is resolved. Their tech support tried to help but couldn’t fix it. Just not worth the hassle.

raw_analyses.title: Good price, but having connection issues
raw_analyses.content:
Holafly offers a competitive price point for its eSIM services, making it an appealing option for travelers who want to stay connected without the hassle of physical SIM cards. I decided to give Holafly a try and purchased a 5-day eSIM plan for use in the United States on my iPad Pro 5G. Initially, the eSIM worked seamlessly once activated, providing a strong and reliable connection. However, a few hours later, I began experiencing intermittent connectivity issues that disrupted my usage. While the affordability of the service is commendable, the reliability of its network performance left much to be desired.

One aspect of Holafly that I found inconvenient was its built-in VPN, which cannot be turned off. This feature seemed to complicate connectivity rather than enhance it, particularly when attempting to use the mobile hotspot feature. Devices connected to the hotspot struggled with extremely slow internet speeds, taking hours to load a single page. This limitation made the hotspot function practically unusable, undermining one of the primary reasons I chose the service. Although Holafly’s pricing and initial performance were promising, the ongoing connectivity issues and technical limitations significantly diminished the overall experience.
